title: At 81, This Gurugram Grandmother Is Still Travelling, Working — and Fully Confident
excerpt: A viral Instagram video by Gurgaon-based founder Mehar Toor shows her 81-year-old grandmother — a businesswoman fresh off an Alaska cruise — explaining her philosophy in one line: she feels fully confident she can go anywhere.
body:
• An Instagram video posted by Gurgaon-based founder Mehar Toor featuring her 81-year-old grandmother has gone viral, with the dadi speaking about work, travel and life on her own terms.
  • The grandmother — a businesswoman and avid traveler — recently returned from an Alaska cruise, which she describes with characteristic understatement: "I have really enjoyed it."
  • Asked how she does it at 81, her answer was simple: "I feel fully confident I can, you know, go anywhere."
  • The exchange has struck a chord online as a portrait of aging on one's own terms — still working, still traveling, still curious.

A conversation, not a lecture

There is no dramatic message in the video. A young founder in Gurgaon turns the camera toward her 81-year-old grandmother and asks a simple question: what has she been up to lately? "Let me introduce to you my 81-year-old grandmother," Mehar Toor says. "She is a businesswoman, an avid traveler still at the age of 81. What's up, Dadi?"

What follows is the kind of conversation families have every day — except this one has been shared widely across the internet. The grandmother talks about her recent travels, her everyday life, and what younger people might learn from her. It is the ordinariness of it that has made it extraordinary online.

The Alaska cruise at 81

The detail that stopped scrollers mid-feed was the cruise. Yes, the 81-year-old dadi recently went on an Alaska cruise. "Yes, I have been to Alaska for my cruise. I have really enjoyed it," she says, with the calm of someone describing a trip to the market. When her granddaughter presses — at 81 years old? — she answers without hesitation: "Yeah, because I feel fully confident I can, you know, go anywhere."

It is worth pausing on that word: confident. Not brave, not adventurous — confident. The confidence of a woman who has run a business, raised a family, and decided long ago that age is a logistical detail, not a verdict.

"I feel fully confident I can, you know, go anywhere."

— Mehar Toor's 81-year-old grandmother, on traveling at 81

Still working, still her own person

The video's quiet power comes from what it doesn't show: no one is marveling at her despite her age. She is introduced first as a businesswoman — still working — and second as a traveler. The traveling is not a bucket-list stunt; it is a continuation of a life she has always lived this way. That framing is what separates this viral moment from the usual inspiration content: she isn't exceptional for her age, she is simply herself, at her age.

Her granddaughter's questions suggest the family treats this as normal, which may be the real story. The dadi who works and travels at 81 usually has people around her who never told her to stop.

Why it resonates

For the diaspora, the dadi is a universal figure — the grandmother on video calls, the one whose health the whole family monitors across time zones. This video flips that script: here is a grandmother nobody needs to worry about, because she has already booked the cruise. It lands as a gentle challenge to every family that has quietly decided what an 81-year-old can and cannot do.

What's next

The video keeps circulating, and the comments keep coming — mostly variations of the same wish: to be her at 81. Her granddaughter hasn't said where the next trip is. Given the Alaska answer, it is probably already planned.
